Merge multiple NICHESObjects into one

Source: R/merge_NICHESObjects.R
merge_NICHESObjects.Rd

Combines a list of NICHESObjects – or any number passed as individual arguments – into a single NICHESObject by concatenating all per-cell and per-edge data. This is the complement to the sample.col splitting that create_NICHESObject performs: it can be used to merge objects that were produced independently and then need to be analyzed together.

Usage

merge_NICHESObjects(..., verbose = TRUE)

Arguments

...

Either (a) multiple NICHESObjects passed directly as positional arguments, or (b) a single named or unnamed list of NICHESObjects, or (c) an explicit list(a, b, c) call.

verbose

Logical. Whether to emit progress messages and warnings. Default TRUE.

Value

A single NICHESObject.

Details

Mode compatibility. All objects must share the same attr(., "mode") ("spatial" or "nonspatial"). A mismatch is a hard error because the slot schemas differ (spatial objects carry x/y in $cell.meta; edge semantics differ).

Barcode uniqueness. Cell barcodes must be globally unique across all objects. If the same barcode string appears in two or more objects the function stops with a clear error. Prepend a sample-specific prefix before constructing the objects (e.g. paste0(sample.id, "_", barcode)) to avoid collisions – Seurat does this automatically via RenameCells().

Gene / LRM union. When gene or LRM lists differ across objects, their union is taken. Genes absent in one object are implicitly zero in $cell.data (which is sparse – zero rows are never stored).

Slot-by-slot strategy:

  • $cell.list, $cell.data, $edge.list, $edge.data – simple concatenation.

  • $cell.meta, $edge.meta – concatenated with fill = TRUE; extra columns in some objects become NA in others.

  • $gene.list, $LRM.list – union.

  • $gene.meta, $LRM.meta – concatenated, deduplicated by key (first occurrence kept).

  • $segmentation – merged via sf::rbind() when all objects have it; NULL with a warning when only some do.

  • Neighborhood slots – always NULL (reserved).

See also

create_NICHESObject for the sample.col argument that automates splitting and merging within one call.

Examples

data(NICHESv2_inputs)
build_sample <- function(cells) {
  create_NICHESObject(
    count.mtx = NICHESv2_inputs$count.mtx[, cells],
    meta.data = NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data[cells, ],
    LRM.db    = NICHESv2_inputs$LRM.db,
    mode      = "spatial",
    k         = 3L,
    verbose   = FALSE
  )
}
barcodes <- rownames(NICHESv2_inputs$meta.data)
obj.s1 <- build_sample(barcodes[1:40])
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 3 | Cells: 40 | Inter-cell: 74 | Autocrine: 40
#> [compute_CellToCell] 114 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 72 non-zero edge signals.
obj.s2 <- build_sample(barcodes[41:80])
#> [create_Edgelist_Spatial] Mode: kNN    | Param: 3 | Cells: 40 | Inter-cell: 84 | Autocrine: 40
#> [compute_CellToCell] 124 edges x 15 LR pairs | method = 'product' | cores = 1
#> [compute_CellToCell] Done. 57 non-zero edge signals.

# Individual objects
merged <- merge_NICHESObjects(obj.s1, obj.s2, verbose = FALSE)

# A pre-built list
obj.list <- list(obj.s1, obj.s2)
merged <- merge_NICHESObjects(obj.list, verbose = FALSE)
